question: For the safest handling on the road, which trailer should be positioned first (immediately behind the tractor) in a set of doubles?
explanation: The more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor; the lighter trailer should be in the rear.

question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A device used only to change tires
choice_c: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: A converter dolly is a coupling device (one or two axles plus a fifth wheel) used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination.

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock brakes?
explanation: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to have antilock brakes, with a yellow lamp on the left side.
source_note: Section 7.1.8 - Antilock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult
choice_b: It is only a minor inconvenience
choice_c: It will trigger the ABS malfunction light
explanation: Unlocking the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer can cause the tow bar to fly up, risking injury and making re-coupling difficult.

question: On a set of doubles, what is the correct position (open or closed) for the shut-off valves at the rear of the FIRST trailer versus the rear of the LAST trailer?
choice_b: Rear of first trailer: OPEN; rear of last trailer: CLOSED
choice_d: Rear of first trailer: CLOSED; rear of last trailer: OPEN
explanation: Shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN; the valve at the rear of the last trailer must be CLOSED.
source_note: Section 7.3.1 - Double and Triple Trailers checks

question: Why must you drive doubles and triples especially smoothly, looking far ahead?
choice_b: It is only a courtesy to other drivers
choice_c: To avoid rollover or jackknife, since doubles/triples are less stable and slower to respond to sudden moves
choice_d: Smoothness has no real safety impact for doubles/triples
explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife; looking far ahead lets you slow or change lanes gradually.

question: When checking that air flows to all trailers in a doubles/triples rig, what should you hear when you open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Nothing; silence confirms the system is charged
choice_b: The ABS malfunction lamp should illuminate
choice_d: Air escaping, confirming the entire system is charged
explanation: You should hear air escaping when opening the emergency line shut-off at the rear of the last trailer, confirming the entire system is charged.
source_note: Section 7.4.1 - Check That Air Flows to All Trailers
